patterns.name: Local service gap
patterns.edge: Demand exists locally but supply is fragmented, expensive, slow, or aimed at larger buyers.

patterns.name: Skill scarcity / translation gap
patterns.edge: A locally scarce skill can transform an existing asset, business process, or customer interface into something more valuable.

patterns.name: Geographic acquisition-resale spread
patterns.edge: The same lawful good has different effective values across places or channels after transport, defects, inventory time, and transaction friction.
common_execution: scale only after observed net spread

patterns.name: Underused asset utilization
patterns.edge: A locally available asset, machine, vehicle, space, dataset, or tool is idle while nearby demand pays for its output or access.

patterns.name: Remote income / local cost-base spread
patterns.edge: A person can sell work into a higher-value market while producing from a lower-cost location, subject to tax, platform, labor, and payment constraints.

patterns.name: Logistics / time-window gap
patterns.edge: Value is lost because supply and demand exist at different times or places and a lawful coordination/logistics layer can bridge them.
